prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a sloped paved street on the left and a sidewalk with a canopy tent on the right as the camera wearer walks forward and turns right across the five frames. In frames 1 and 2, a woman walking ahead on the right is very bright at roughly 1 to 1.5 m away (within or near arm's reach in frame 2 as a closer companion enters on the bottom right at under 1 m), while a man in black stands about 3 to 4 m ahead to her left, facing right and slightly toward the wearer in frame 2, and a parked truck sits 15 to 20 m away on the far left. From frames 3 to 5, the wearer passes between the man in black (2 to 3 m on the left) and the companion (roughly 1 m in front/left, facing away and occluding the parked SUV 5 to 7 m behind her), while approaching the tent canopy (1.5 to 2.5 m on the right) where three seated staff and a seated visitor are arranged 0.5 to 1 m apart around a table at 2.5 to 4 m depth with items on the table within their arm's reach. This map clarifies the continuous ground plane gradient and the distinct depth layering between the foreground companion, the tent frame, and the recessed interior occupants that blend into the shadowed tent in RGB. However, the depth map is unreliable on distant background buildings and sky (which collapse to uniform black), blurs the top of the woman's head in frame 1, and flattens fine tabletop objects and open tent wall gaps into smooth grey surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and mid-ground instances against an unlabelled black background as the camera wearer advances along the sidewalk and turns toward the tent on the right. In frame 1, it labels the woman 1.5 m ahead in white with a handbag at her left hip, the man in black 3.5 m to her left, a distant pedestrian 10 m above on the hillside stairs, a truck 15 m left, and a car partially occluded on the right edge; in frames 2 to 5, a companion wearing a backpack stays 0.5 to 1.5 m in front and shifts to the left edge while facing away. Inside the tent on the right in frames 3 to 5 (2.5 to 4 m away), the masks separate up to four seated people facing one another across a central dining table, along with a chair and a cup within their arm's reach, partially occluded by the tent walls and by the foreground companion on the left. The segmentation map makes it easier than RGB alone to distinguish individual overlapping seated figures inside the shadowed tent and to spot small distant vehicles and pedestrians on the upper slope. However, it is unreliable in class labelling and temporal consistency: it misclassifies the tent canopy as a 'truck' in frame 3, drops it completely in frame 4, and relabels it as an 'airplane' in frame 5, while missing the man in black in frame 2 and fragmenting masks around occluded lower bodies.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D yellow body skeletons on a black background only in frames 1 and 2, failing to detect any people in frames 3 through 5. In frame 1, a single truncated torso-and-head skeleton represents the woman in the white shirt about 1.5 m directly ahead on the right, showing her shoulders square and facing away from the camera wearer with her right arm angled down toward her side and her lower legs cut off by the bottom frame edge. In frame 2, that woman is no longer tracked, and a single full-body profile skeleton appears for the man in black standing roughly 3 m ahead to the left, oriented sideways facing right with his head and torso turned slightly toward the camera wearer and his hands resting near hip level within his own arm's reach. While the skeletons make the torso orientation of the woman in frame 1 and the side-profile stance and limb joints of the man in frame 2 explicit without background clutter, the map provides no distance metric or scene layout on its own. It is highly unreliable across the sequence, missing all magenta hand skeletons, failing to detect the very close companion in frames 2 to 5, the man in black in frames 1 and 3, and all seated people inside the tent in frames 3 to 5 due to close-range truncation and table/tent occlusion.
